sections.h2: Where does Henderson County record deeds?
sections.html:
Find the Register of Deeds inside the Henderson County Courthouse, 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. It records documents Monday through Friday between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM, and the main phone is 828-697-4901.

Staff describe the counter as a recording office. They check that a document follows the North Carolina Real Estate Recording Standards, but they cannot advise anyone in a legal capacity, so questions about what a deed should say go to your closing attorney. Payment may be by check, cash, money order or card, and a card payment adds a vendor fee that goes to the vendor.

The Tax Department's Land Records section works from the same courthouse. It builds the county's official index of tax listings from the deeds the register records and from Clerk of Court files, so a deed that reaches the register soon shows up in the parcel data the county uses for billing.

sections.h2: Which documents sit in the Henderson County deed vault?
sections.html:
Land transactions in the county are archived here. Its published list of holdings:

  • Land transfers, easements, rights of way and surveys
  • Deeds of trust, mortgages and UCC filings
  • Separation agreements
  • Assumed business name (DBA) filings
  • Notary public oaths
  • Vital records, with certified copies at $10.00 and photocopies at $.25
  • Military records, recorded and certified for the veteran at no charge

Marriage licenses are by appointment only, between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM on weekdays, and the county asks callers to phone rather than email. The assumed business name page adds a warning that forms must be printed on one side of the paper only. Printing front and back does not meet recording requirements and brings a non-standard document fee on top of recording fees.

sections.h2: How can I search Henderson County deeds and plats online?
sections.html:
The county offers an online deed index that runs from 1979 to the present, hosted by a records vendor. Visitors accept a disclaimer first, and the site works best on a desktop or laptop with Chrome or Edge, cookies on and pop-up blocking off for the site.

To pull a plat, open the Register of Deeds system and choose View Images. Pick Plat as the book type, then enter the recording year or Cabinet A, B or C as the book, and the plat number as the page. Leading zeros are not needed. The county's guide lists slide ranges by year. Recent years run like this:

  • 2021: slides 12982 to 13869
  • 2022: slides 13870 to 14600
  • 2023: slides 14601 to 15329
  • 2024: slides 15330 to 16020
  • 2025: slides 16021 to 16768
  • 2026: slide 16769 onward

Older plats from 1988 forward follow the same numbering, with three early cabinets covering the oldest slides.

The site's own disclaimer says the register makes no guarantee about the accuracy of the online images and that the official records stay in the courthouse office, so confirm anything important at the counter. A privacy notice on the search page cites G.S. 132-1.8(g). A document filed for recording should leave out Social Security, driver license, bank account and card numbers unless the law requires them. Anyone can ask the register in writing to remove such a number from an online image, and no fee is charged for that request.

sections.h2: What are the statutory recording amounts in Henderson County?
sections.html:
State law sets the recording amounts, so Henderson County follows G.S. 161-10.

Statewide recording amounts from G.S. 161-10 that apply in Henderson County
DocumentStatute amount
General instrument$26.00 for 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee

Ask the office about any local charge for services outside recording. The statute text is at G.S. 161-10.

sections.h2: Who covers the deed stamp tax when a Henderson house sells?
sections.html:
The seller does, as the transferor named in the statute. The rate is $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or fraction of it, and the register collects it first.

Look for it on the settlement statement ahead of closing day. The statute is at G.S. 105-228.30.

sections.h2: What does the 2027 reappraisal mean for a Henderson County seller?
sections.html:
Values reset on January 1, 2027. Henderson County reappraises real property every four years, well ahead of the eight-year minimum set by G.S. 105-286, and the last reappraisal took effect in 2023.

The county says values follow market prices from recent qualified sales, and that a mass appraisal groups similar properties together. It weighs location, construction type, age, replacement cost and zoning. Buildings still under construction on January 1 are valued by their percentage of completion. Land enrolled in the Present-Use Value Program for agriculture, horticulture or forestry can carry an assessed value below market value.

The Tax Department counts about 71,500 parcels, and property taxes make up an estimated 50 percent of the county operating budget in fiscal year 2027. The Board of Commissioners sets the rate and the Assessor sets values. Its Tax Department page lists divisions for real property, personal property, exemptions and deferment, land records and collections. The county's programs cover elderly or disabled owners, disabled veterans, nonprofits, commercial farms and wildlife management. See the county reappraisal page.

sections.h2: How big is the Henderson County housing market?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Henderson County at 122,375 people in July 2025, which is 5.2 percent above the April 2020 base, spread over 372.95 square miles of land. There were 61,173 housing units, and builders pulled 1,093 permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 75.0 percent of homes, valued at $351,400 in the middle of the 2020 to 2024 range. Monthly owner costs are $1,608 with a mortgage and $482 without. Tenants face gross rent near $1,187, and household income sits at $68,187 across 51,067 households of 2.29 people.

Age shapes sales here. Adults past 65 are 29.1 percent of residents, and the survey counts 7,811 veterans. The property tax exclusions for older, disabled and veteran owners are worth a question to the Tax Department. See Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What should I prepare before recording a deed in Henderson County?
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps the document from being flagged or delayed at the counter.

  • Print on one side of letter or legal paper in black ink, using at least 10 point type.
  • State the instrument type across the head of page one and leave a three inch blank margin there.
  • Redact Social Security and account numbers unless the law requires them.
  • Put the drafter's name and the parcel number on page one.
  • Have your attorney file the satisfaction of any paid-off deed of trust.

If the deed fails the formatting standards, the register records it anyway after collecting an added nonstandard document fee. Staff can also issue a certified copy of anything the office recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed in Henderson County?
faqs.a: The county lists appointments only for marriage licenses, which run 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM and are booked by phone. Recording is open during the regular weekday window, and the office takes questions at 828-697-4901.

faqs.q: How far back does the Henderson County online deed index go?
faqs.a: The online index covers 1979 to the present. Older plats are found by choosing Plat as the book type and entering a year or Cabinet A, B or C. Check the county's plat guide for the slide ranges.

faqs.q: Does Henderson County reappraise property every year?
faqs.a: No. The county reappraises real property every four years, last in 2023, with the next reappraisal effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one at least every eight years.

faqs.q: Can I pay by card at the Henderson County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards are accepted along with checks, cash and money orders. The vendor that processes the card adds a fee, and Henderson County does not charge it.

faqs.q: What does a certified vital record cost in Henderson County?
faqs.a: A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate is $10.00 with proper ID and an acceptable relationship to the person named. Photocopies are $.25.
